questions.question: Which workload most strongly favors a relational database transaction?
options: A payment ledger that must update an order and payment record together
A disposable image cache
A lookup of one session by its known ID
A static file archive
questions.explanation: A relational transaction and constraints are a strong fit when related records must preserve a business invariant together.

questions.question: A support engineer needs every order to have exactly one customer while allowing a customer to keep years of order history. Which schema best enforces that relationship?
options: Add one mutable order_id column to customers
Add a non-null customer_id foreign key to orders
Store order IDs as a comma-separated customers field
Create an order_customer table without uniqueness constraints
questions.explanation: The foreign key belongs on the many side, so each order names one valid customer and the database can enforce ownership. A customer.order_id column is tempting but can represent only one order and would overwrite history.

questions.question: A transfer debits Account A, then the credit to Account B fails. Which property should ensure neither balance changes?
options: Atomicity
Consistency
Isolation
Durability
questions.explanation: Atomicity makes the related writes one all-or-nothing unit, so the database rolls the debit back when the credit cannot complete.

questions.question: What type of database is MySQL?
options: NoSQL document database
Relational SQL database
Key-value store
Graph database
questions.explanation: MySQL is a popular open-source relational database management system that uses SQL for querying and supports ACID transactions.

questions.question: Which statement best captures PostgreSQL's durability boundary?
options: A transaction is durable when every changed heap page is written immediately
A transaction can be acknowledged after its required WAL record is durable, even if data pages are written later
A transaction is durable when a read replica applies it
A transaction is durable when autovacuum observes it
questions.explanation: Write-ahead logging records changes before dirty data pages. Crash recovery replays durable WAL, so the acknowledgement policy is tied to WAL durability rather than immediate heap-page writes.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the lesson's core document-modeling invariant?
options: Every relationship should be embedded to avoid joins
Data that must change atomically should live in one bounded document; cross-document consistency needs an explicit mechanism
Flexible schema removes the need for validation
Every collection should use the same document shape
questions.explanation: Single-document writes are atomic, so the document is the natural consistency boundary. Growth and independent ownership still determine whether embedding remains safe.
